source.title: The Mechanism of Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Feature Elicitation from Latent Knowledge

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes and numerically studies weak-to-strong feature elicitation, but its outcomes are feature-alignment measures rather than task performance or PGR. It therefore does not directly test any of the listed performance-focused versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical and synthetic results on target-feature alignment and preservation or loss of off-target features. These do not measure whether the student beats the weak supervisor in task performance or how PGR changes. The paper’s claims about surpassing the weak model are formalized as acquiring and retaining feature directions, not as a measured performance comparison.
record.test_reason: A theory paper on V5. It proves conditions (two-layer polynomial nets, subspace prior, even target link, inputs concentrated on the target subspace, off-target localization χk small) under which first-layer W2S SGD gains the target feature while keeping off-target features the weak model lacks. The authors define this as the student surpassing the weak model. A small synthetic run confirms it. It measures feature alignment, not task performance or PGR, so V1–V4 and V6 are not tested. The record said 'tests' yet marked every version not_tested; V5 is the version these results bear on.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also define W2S success specifically as the strong model acquiring θκ while retaining off-target features the task-specialized weak model lacks. They note that the analysis is first-layer, feature-level only, and that the forgetting result is specific to the SFT algorithm studied.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a theoretical two-layer polynomial-network reward-model setup with task-specific subspaces, online SGD, a nonlinear transformation of clipped weak-model outputs, and a task-concentrated input distribution. It does not reproduce the original empirical language-model fine-tuning or measure PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: The stated guarantees depend on the even target link, subspace-concentrated input distribution, weak-model errors, initialization and Hermite-sign conditions, and off-target localization χk; the paper notes that odd links do not provide the same preservation result.

fits_no_version.finding: Under SFT on direct labels with isotropic inputs, off-target neurons whose features correlate with the target align with the target before the target neurons converge (≈0.8 in the synthetic run).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a two-layer synthetic setting, standard SFT causes forgetting of correlated off-target features, while W2S preserves them.

record.problems: The theory concerns two-layer polynomial networks and feature alignment, not Transformers or measured reward/task performance. The authors state that second-layer learning and preservation of off-target reward quality are not formally analyzed; the forgetting result is algorithm-specific. The numerical experiment reports a single configuration and no error bars or repeated-run uncertainty.

untested.parts: No weak-supervisor score, strong ceiling or PGR; there is no task-performance comparison at all.
No auxiliary-confidence, ensembling or loss-variant comparison. The clipping/exp transformation is part of the analyzed algorithm, not compared against naive W2S.
No variation of supervisor or student size or of task; one synthetic configuration.
No exploitation, distribution shift or error-correlation analysis. The SFT forgetting result concerns SFT, not W2S failure.
Second-layer learning and function-level (reward-quality) guarantees are not analyzed; Transformers not covered.

missing.what: Argument that with an odd target link (GE=1) a constant gradient term drives off-target neurons toward θκ, so preservation (and hence the surpassing argument) fails.

Statement that the student's achievable target alignment error is bounded below by Es (weak model L1 and alignment error plus off-subspace mass): the student does not beat the weak model on task κ itself.

record.verdict_notes: Pure theory plus one CPU synthetic run. Relation and tranche are kept at 'tests'/T2 for V5 only. The record's version statuses (all not_tested) contradicted its own relation field and are corrected here.

versions.untested_parts: No weak-supervisor task score, strong-model true-label ceiling, or PGR is measured.
No comparison of auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling, or loss variants against naive fine-tuning.
The paper studies one synthetic reward-model setting and theoretical subspace conditions, but does not measure PGR across sizes, tasks, or representations.
No test of exploitation beyond supervisor checking, distribution shift, or shared weak/strong errors.
The theorems establish feature-alignment and preservation guarantees under assumptions, not conditions that guarantee the student beats its supervisor in task performance.
No vision or other non-language modality is tested.

relationships.condition: Two-layer polynomial networks, first-layer online SGD, even target link, input distribution concentrated on the target subspace, off-target localization χk ≤ 1/polylog(d)
relationships.reason: R1/R2 prove that the student gains the target feature and keeps off-target features, and R4/R5 confirm this in one synthetic run. But 'surpassing' holds only at the feature level, and target alignment cannot beat the weak model's error Es. Remark 2 says it fails for odd links.
relationships.display_finding: Target-feature elicitation and off-target preservation are proved and confirmed in a synthetic run, while target alignment cannot improve beyond weak-model error Eₛ; odd links can fail.

relation.reason: The paper supplies its own theoretical results and synthetic checks of a feature-level W2S mechanism.

tranche.reason: A different theoretical method directly studies W2S feature learning and preservation through multi-step SGD.

source_check.notes: The paper defines surpassing through acquiring the target feature while retaining features absent from the specialist weak model; it does not establish superior target-task reward performance. The approximate experimental alignments are explicitly stated in the prose, despite the rows' figure_only locators.

statements.correction: Even-link setting: target-feature elicitation and off-target preservation hold under the stated assumptions. Synthetic setting: d = 1024; s = 128; η = 0.2; T = 10000; target alignment ≈ 0.95; off-target alignment ≈ 1.0. Remark 2: GE = 1 produces off-target drift and forgetting. Reward-quality superiority and second-layer learning are not established.
statements.problem: The factual summary matches the text, but the limits_scope label mixes successful even-link conditions with odd-link failure outside that condition group. Function-level guarantees are untested.
